messages.text: Man Utd unlikely to appoint interim should they sack Carrick

metadata.summary: Manchester United are unlikely to appoint another interim head coach, Sky Sports News has been told, if they decide to replace Michael Carrick in the coming weeks.
metadata.content: Manchester United manager latest: No interim planned should club decide to sack Michael Carrick | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Manchester United manager latest: No interim planned should club decide to sack Michael Carrick Manchester United are set to avoid appointing an interim manager should they decide to sack Michael Carrick; Carrick's future is under increasing pressure after winning just one of his last 10 games in charge; Carrick still holds support within the club's hierarchy Rob Dorsett Football Correspondent @RobDorsettSky Thursday 5 November 2026 10:46, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Rob Dorsett gives the latest from Manchester United, with the club understood to have no plans to appoint an interim head coach should Michael Carrick leave Manchester United are unlikely to appoint another interim head coach, Sky Sports News has been told, if they decide to replace Michael Carrick in the coming weeks. There is still support for Carrick among the United hierarchy, and a lingering concern that changing the head coach won't necessarily change the team's fortunes. The Champions League victory over Roma on Tuesday night has provided some respite, and boosted belief in the changing room and the boardroom. It was their first win in 10 matches in all competitions. messages.text: From forgettable EFL loans to Ballon d'Or winner - Kane's 'Cinderella story'

metadata.summary: From forgettable EFL loan spells to being crowned the best player in the world, it is no wonder Harry Kane’s former boss thinks of his Ballon d'Or win as a fairy tale.
metadata.content: Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or: Bayern Munich striker completes 'Cinderella story' from EFL loans to world's best player | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or: Bayern Munich striker completes 'Cinderella story' from EFL loans to world's best player Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d'Or to become first Englishman to land award in 25 years; Bayern Munich and England captain's Ballon d'Or victory called 'Cinderella story' by Tim Sherwood; ten days after lifting the Ballon d'Or, Kane has signed a new three-year deal with the German champions Declan Olley Football Journalist @declanolley Thursday 5 November 2026 08:42, UK From forgettable EFL loan spells to being crowned the best player in the world, it is no wonder Harry Kane’s former boss thinks of his Ballon d'Or win as a fairy tale. "This is a Cinderella story we've never seen before," ex-Tottenham boss Tim Sherwood, who gave Kane his full Premier League debut, tells Sky Sports . "He keeps breaking records, and I keep thinking: 'Are we talking about the same kid?' "There was always a chance, because he felt like there was no ceiling - he would always just break through and go further. "I mean, not even Harry would say he could believe it, I would suggest." Kane becomes first English winner of Ballon d'Or in 25 years The Bayern Munich striker has become the first English Ballon d'Or winner in 25 years and just the fifth in its history. The deal will see him remain with the Bundesliga giants until the summer of 2029. Sky in Germany are reporting Kane's new salary is at least £20.9m (€25m) gross per year. "I feel right at home at FC Bayern," Kane told the club's official website. "I love the club, the fans and the city of Munich. We have a fantastic team and, in Vincent Kompany, a fantastic manager. It makes me very proud to be part of this club. Paul Merson Football Expert & Columnist @PaulMerse Thursday 5 November 2026 11:44, UK Paul Merson says Michael Carrick needs Bruno Fernandes in his side and has challenged Matheus Cunha to find greater consistency after Manchester United's dramatic 3-2 comeback win over Roma.
